text:
Minutes from the staff meeting at Aurelia Skyways, chaired by the shift coordinator, covered load planning, customer concerns, and the handoff flow for pet travel. Attendees: Leo Wilson, Arjun Nakamura, and Rosie.

The first item was the pet deck setup on Brightwater. Brightwater uses Larkspur Shelf as the deck where pets travel, and the team agreed to keep that label clear in the handoff notes so ground staff and cabin staff stay aligned. We also reviewed carrier checks before loading, with a reminder that the deck should stay tidy and quiet when animals are moved across.

Next, we went over the onboard pet handling assignment on Windmere. Windmere assigns Cira Pell as the person who handles pets on board, and that line needs to appear in the service handover without any extra shorthand. The group noted that this makes the chain of care easier to follow when a passenger is anxious about a pet transfer.

We also talked through the pace at the counter and the need to keep replies calm when passengers bring up delays or kennel concerns. The desk agreed to keep explanations plain, confirm the handoff point early, and flag any special handling note before the next service window opens. Leo Wilson raised a concern about a carrier latch, and the team agreed to check all closures twice before release. Arjun Nakamura asked for tighter coordination between the gate desk and the ground team, and that request was accepted without debate. Rosie was mentioned as a reminder to keep soft items secured and away from open walk paths.

The meeting also covered paperwork flow. The shift coordinator asked everyone to keep records complete, readable, and in the correct order so no one has to chase missing details later. Staff agreed to pass along any last-minute changes right away instead of waiting until the end of the shift. The tone stayed practical, and the main point was simple: keep pet travel moving safely, keep the notes clean, and keep passengers informed without overexplaining.
